In Q1 2026, Baidu Intelligent Cloud's growth rate reached 79%, ranking first among China's leading cloud vendors. At the Baidu Developer Conference in May, Yin Yingli, Vice President of Baidu Intelligent Cloud and General Manager of the Channel Ecosystem Department, disclosed that 10% of core partners achieved business growth exceeding that of Baidu Intelligent Cloud as a whole. Over the past year or more, Baidu Intelligent Cloud's channel ecosystem has undergone significant changes in partner classification, scenario focus, and revenue distribution mechanisms.

The changes began in April 2025, when Yin Yingli had just taken office as General Manager of Baidu Intelligent Cloud's Channel Ecosystem Department. Examining the channel ecosystem's assets, the thousands of partners seemed numerous, but most relationships remained at the project level. What was called an ecosystem was more like a temporary alliance, not a lasting partnership. This model worked in the project-based cloud computing era: partners sold resources, vendors gave rebates, and everyone got what they needed. But after AI arrived, customers no longer wanted just cloud resources and cloud products—they wanted AI solutions that directly solved business problems. Previously, channels could do well with just reselling and customer relationships, but that no longer works.

This shift in demand has forced cloud vendors to rethink a question: how exactly should the partner ecosystem be managed? Shen Dou, Executive Vice President of Baidu Group and President of Baidu Intelligent Cloud Business Group, has a clear judgment on this: "Industrial intelligence is a long-term process, and its core lies in 'providing the foundation and empowering partners.'" In his view, the ten-trillion-yuan market opportunity embedded in the three-tier architecture of computing power, models, and applications belongs to all ecosystem partners deeply engaged in their respective industries.
excerpt_i18n.es: En el Q1 de 2026, la velocidad de crecimiento de Baidu Smart Cloud alcanzó el 79%, la más alta entre los principales proveedores de nube de China. En la Conferencia de Desarrolladores de Baidu de mayo, Yin Yingli, vicepresidente de Baidu Smart Cloud y gerente general del Departamento de Ecosistema de Canales, reveló que el 10% de los socios principales superaron en crecimiento a la media de Baidu Smart Cloud. Durante el último año y medio, el ecosistema de canales de Baidu Smart Cloud ha experimentado cambios notables en la clasificación de socios, el enfoque en escenarios y el mecanismo de distribución de beneficios. Los cambios comenzaron en abril de 2025. En aquel momento, Yin Yingli acababa de asumir el cargo de gerente general del Departamento de Ecosistema de Canales de Baidu Smart Cloud. Al revisar los recursos del ecosistema de canales, los miles de socios parecían no ser pocos, pero la mayoría de las relaciones seguían limitándose a proyectos.
